## Comparability note

Alaska Air Group's FY2024 revenue is **not** directly comparable to its FY2022/FY2023 revenue: Alaska completed its acquisition of Hawaiian Holdings on September 18, 2024, and "[t]he results of Hawaiian are included in the consolidated financial statements beginning September 18, 2024," contributing "$869 million" of revenue from the acquisition date through December 31, 2024 [DOC-2]. I therefore compute Alaska's growth on an ex-Hawaiian basis: $11,735M − $869M = **$10,866M** of legacy-Alaska revenue in FY2024 [DOC-1][DOC-2]. (This is a partial-year carve-out only; it removes Hawaiian's stub-period revenue but does not adjust for any integration effects on legacy Alaska.) The other four carriers are all calendar-year filers with no acquisition adjustment noted [DOC-1].

## FY2023 → FY2024 revenue growth

| Rank | Airline | FY2023 | FY2024 | Growth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | United | $53,717M | $57,063M | **+6.23%** |
| 2 | Delta | $58,048M | $61,643M | **+6.19%** |
| 3 | Southwest | $26,091M | $27,483M | **+5.34%** |
| 4 | Alaska (ex-Hawaiian) | $10,426M | $10,866M | **+4.22%** |
| 5 | American | $52,788M | $54,211M | **+2.70%** |

Source figures: Delta $58,048M → $61,643M; United $53,717M → $57,063M; Southwest $26,091M → $27,483M; American $52,788M → $54,211M; Alaska $10,426M → $11,735M reported [DOC-1], less $869M Hawaiian [DOC-2].

Note: United and Delta are separated by only ~3 basis points — effectively a tie.

## FY2022 → FY2024 revenue growth

| Rank | Airline | FY2022 | FY2024 | Growth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | United | $44,955M | $57,063M | **+26.9%** |
| 2 | Delta | $50,582M | $61,643M | **+21.9%** |
| 3 | Southwest | $23,814M | $27,483M | **+15.4%** |
| 4 | Alaska (ex-Hawaiian) | $9,646M | $10,866M | **+12.6%** |
| 5 | American | $48,971M | $54,211M | **+10.7%** |

Source figures: Delta FY2022 $50,582M; United $44,955M; Southwest $23,814M; American $48,971M; Alaska $9,646M [DOC-1]; Alaska FY2024 adjusted for the $869M Hawaiian contribution [DOC-2].

## Conclusion

Yes — **United Airlines Holdings ranks first in both rankings** (+6.23% one-year and +26.9% two-year), though its one-year lead over Delta is within rounding significance. The full ordering is identical across both periods except that American and Alaska swap relative positions only in the sense that both remain in the bottom two; in fact the order (United, Delta, Southwest, Alaska, American) is the same in both windows.

ANSWER: FY23→FY24: United +6.23%, Delta +6.19%, Southwest +5.34%, Alaska (ex-Hawaiian) +4.22%, American +2.70%. FY22→FY24: United +26.9%, Delta +21.9%, Southwest +15.4%, Alaska (ex-Hawaiian) +12.6%, American +10.7%. Yes — United is top-ranked in both (Alaska adjusted to exclude $869M of acquired Hawaiian revenue; United's one-year edge over Delta is only ~3bps).
